## ⚠️ Diagnostic probe — DO NOT MERGE, DO NOT REVIEW

This PR exists to make CI answer one question. It will be **closed as soon as the `components` job reports**, merged never. It is not a proposal to take the dependency bump — that is [#18325](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/18325), whose commit is carried here unchanged and unowned.

**Contents:** `dependabot/npm_and_yarn/all-deps-14f5d95444@29f380f097` (unmodified) + one fixture commit from [`ada/18331-pass-stamp`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/tree/ada/18331-pass-stamp).

## Why CI has to answer it

`#18331` fails deterministically in CI on the bumped tree and is green on its base. It does **not** reproduce locally — four independent configurations, all green:

| configuration | result |
|---|---|
| macOS arm64, failing spec alone | 7/7 pass |
| macOS arm64, full `components` suite | 182/182, exit 0 |
| Linux arm64 (`playwright:v1.62.1-noble`), failing spec alone | 7/7 pass |
| Linux arm64, full suite, `--cpus=2` | 236 passed, exit 0 |

Untried axis: **x86_64**, which is what `ubuntu-latest` runs. A broken build artifact would fail on every platform; a failure that only appears on one is the signature of a **race**, not a bad chunk.

So the mechanism has to be read where it actually fires. The `components` job captures no app-worker console output — proven earlier by grepping a run where the mechanism demonstrably occurred and finding zero lines — so a `console.warn` cannot carry the answer out. The **assertion message** is the only channel that reaches a reader on a loaded runner, which is what this commit changes.

## What it will report

Both stacks on the duplicate were previously frame-for-frame identical (`module` → `#loadModuleOnce` → `Card.loadModule` → `BodyContainer.insert` → `Reconciler.mjs:856`), so the call site cannot separate the two candidate mechanisms. `Reconciler#reconcileProjection` builds `resolvedItems` per call and writes the inserted instance back, so it dedupes **within** a pass and has no memory **across** one — making the pass, not the caller, the discriminator.

Each request now names its pass, so the failure message resolves it directly:

| what the message shows | what it means |
|---|---|
| two different `[pass N]` ids | cross-pass — the memo legitimately does not span them (@neo-opus-grace's hypothesis, **observed** rather than inferred) |
| the same `[pass N]` twice | within-pass — something defeats the memo, and her hypothesis is dead |
| `[pass N REPAIR]` | the request came from `onDockProjectionFailed`'s one clean re-projection |
| `OVERLAP[...]` | two passes in flight at request time — a third mechanism neither of us proposed |

That converts AC-3 from elimination into observation, which is the boundary the ticket is currently stuck at.

## Evidence

`Evidence: L2 achieved (fixture-only instrument, 5/5 clean local runs on dev; insert arm's numbered-pass assertion held 10/10) → L2 required (the instrument is a test witness, not a behaviour change; no src/ file is touched)`

The stamp is proven on the **green** path because the run it exists for leaves no session to attach to: the insert arm asserts a *numbered* pass, since a stamp that never populated would render `[no active pass]` and read exactly like the within-pass answer.

One measurement worth recording regardless of this PR's outcome: over 10 local runs the **activation** route raises its request outside any projection 8 times and inside `[pass 2]` twice — activation and projection are not serialized against each other. That is **not** this ticket's mechanism (the CI duplicate arrives via `insert` on both requests), so the arm pins only the rendering rather than encoding an 80%-true accident as a contract.
